title: Wringer decisions — the plain-language companion to a spec
description: A `wringer.decisions.v1` document (SPEC_PMPLAN_V0). Source, not evidence: it lives in the repository beside `wringer.spec.yaml`. It exists because `wringer.spec.v1` is frozen and `additionalProperties: false`, so none of this has a home in it — and because a version spend on the spec ripples through every reader of every archived bundle, where a new file touches only what opts in (law 7). NO AUTHORITY OVER WHAT IS BUILT: no gate here runs, nothing under `.wringer/` is written from it, and no builder is ever briefed from it. Its `consent` block can make `wring plan` REFUSE, and refusing is the only thing it can do. ALL THREE BLOCKS ARE DECLARED HERE AND ALL THREE ARE OPTIONAL, deliberately: this file freezes on publication, so declaring only what has a producer today would force a version spend the moment the next one arrives — later work adds producers and never a byte. The `wringer.acceptance.v3` precedent covers the gap, provided it is named where a reader meets it, so: AT PUBLICATION, `assumptions` is written by `wring spec` and `outcomes` and `consent` HAVE NO WRITER. `consent` in particular describes a hand-edit check that was ruled OWED after review — the shape is reserved, the behaviour is not built, and no reader should infer from this file that a spec's answers have been fingerprinted.

assumptions.description: Decisions the drafter took INSTEAD of asking. Measured 2026-08-19: told to prefer visible assumptions and given no field to put one in, a drafter writes them into a criterion's test `guidance`, where the person approving the plan never reads them as decisions — 14 criteria across four replies to one unchanged PRD. This is the field that was missing. Approving the plan approves these.

id.description: A slug, obeying the frozen open-question id rule BYTE FOR BYTE: `wringer-board revise` promotes an assumption into `open_questions`, so an id this file accepted and the spec loader would not is a spec the engine then refuses, leaving a person a broken file and an error about a document they never hand-edited.

decision.description: One plain sentence: what was decided.

why.description: One plain sentence: why it was decided that way.

instead_of_asking.description: The question the person would otherwise have been asked. REQUIRED, and it is what stops this channel becoming a tidier place to hide a decision than `guidance` was: carrying the displaced question means the person is always one action away from asking it after all.

outcomes.description: One plain-language sentence per task: what the person will be able to DO when that task is done, beside the machine `objective` the engineer works from. NO WRITER AT PUBLICATION — the producer arrives with the plan's two registers.

task.description: The id of a task in `wringer.spec.yaml`. A row naming a task the spec does not have is refused whole — content pointing at nothing, the same rule the gate sidecar applies to a `proves` naming no criterion.

consent.description: What the approver approved, recorded at the moment they approved it, so that a spec edited afterwards can be told from one that was not. NO WRITER AT PUBLICATION: the check was ruled OWED after review, because it would need one implementation in the engine and another in the board — two packages with no shared code and no dependency edge — over a canonical form that any normalisation difference would turn into `wring plan` accusing an honest person of editing their spec after approving it. The shape is reserved; the behaviour is not built. Absence of this block is NOT evidence of tampering and never becomes so: a spec approved by hand never claimed a fingerprint.

fingerprint.description: Digest over the canonical serialisation of every question id with its answer and every assumption id with its decision. Prefixed with its algorithm, so a later one can arrive without a version spend.
